initialObservation.roomText: Rows of yellow, red, pink, and white roses fill the garden beside the house. There are holes in the soft earth near your feet. A wooden ladder rests beside the rose beds.
initialObservation.caseIntroduction: Marshall Robner was found dead in the Library. His death appears to be suicide, but you, the investigating inspector, are not convinced. You will examine the scene and question the household. Robner had been taking a medicine called Ebullion.

suspects.name: Ms. S. Dunbar
suspects.detail: Robner's secretary; she has worked for him for about ten years.

actionGuide.description: Move to another room.
Look at a visible object, person, document, or piece of evidence already found.
Search around objects for details, hidden items, or counts. Search a person's belongings during a private interview.
Question a suspect about a subject.
Speak privately with a suspect; the officer stays with the others.
End the private interview and return the suspect to the group.
Present found evidence to a suspect who is with you.
Shade a writing surface to bring out faint marks.
Send found evidence for laboratory analysis.
Compare two evidence items. Either order is accepted.
Name a suspect who is present. If an episode limit does not end the game, choose to close the case or continue investigating.

history.message: Baxter agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.

Baxter consents to the search. Among his belongings, you find a Hartford Philharmonic ticket dated July 7, 1982, for 8 p.m., Row R, Seat 7. Its time matches the preliminary estimate of Robner's death.
“Dunbar was with me at the concert. She became ill and left at intermission in a hired car.”
The private interview with Baxter ends. Baxter returns to the officer and the group.
Dunbar agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.

Dunbar consents to the search. You find a bottle of LoBlo among her belongings and a Hartford Philharmonic ticket dated July 7, 1982, for 8 p.m., Row R, Seat 8. Its time matches the preliminary estimate of Robner's death. Row R, Seat 8 is beside Baxter's Seat 7; the two were seated together.
“Baxter and I attended the concert. He was with me, and he took me home after it ended.”
The private interview with Dunbar ends. Dunbar returns to the officer and the group.
George agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.
The private interview with George ends. George returns to the officer and the group.
Mrs. Robner agrees to speak with you privately. The officer stays with the others.
Among Mrs. Robner's belongings is a bottle labeled Allergone.
The private interview with Mrs. Robner ends. Mrs. Robner returns to the officer and the group.
You enter the kitchen.
Each piece is hand-painted with a scene from Greek mythology.
There are six hand-painted cups and seven hand-painted saucers in the cabinet.
There are eight large and small plates, seven saucers, and six cups.
You enter the garden.
There are two holes in the soft earth, each about two inches by four inches and at least three inches deep. The soil around them is compacted.
The wooden ladder is about fifteen feet long and caked with dirt and dried mud. Its feet seem to fit the holes in the garden.
Digging in the soft earth, you cut your finger on a sharp edge and find a piece of porcelain covered in dirt and dried mud.
The porcelain fragment is covered in dried mud, with its design difficult to make out.
As you wipe off the porcelain, its hand-painted design becomes visible. The markings match the china you examined in the Kitchen.
The lab finds traces of tea and sugar, along with another chemical not commonly used as medication. It is not Amitraxin (Ebullion). No clear fingerprints remain.

events.message:
“Dear Leslie,

I am sorry to hear that Marshall is despondent again. I know how much his troubles weigh on you, and I wish I could be there to comfort you. His despondency is tied to his business. He speaks of suicide when he is in this state, but the thought of what will happen to the company may keep him going.

So George has made his threats again? It is hard to believe he could cause Marshall so much pain. If the worst should happen, you will be provided for as you deserve.

I look forward to Friday, when we can be together again. Until then, remember how much I love you and the life we hope to share.

Love,
Steven”

You enter the kitchen.
Each piece is hand-painted with a scene from Greek mythology.
There are six hand-painted cups and seven hand-painted saucers in the cabinet.
There are eight large and small plates, seven saucers, and six cups.
You enter the garden.
There are two holes in the soft earth, each about two inches by four inches and at least three inches deep. The soil around them is compacted.
The wooden ladder is about fifteen feet long and caked with dirt and dried mud. Its feet seem to fit the holes in the garden.
Digging in the soft earth, you cut your finger on a sharp edge and find a piece of porcelain covered in dirt and dried mud.
The porcelain fragment is covered in dried mud, with its design difficult to make out.
As you wipe off the porcelain, its hand-painted design becomes visible. The markings match the china you examined in the Kitchen.
The lab finds traces of tea and sugar, along with another chemical not commonly used as medication. It is not Amitraxin (Ebullion). No clear fingerprints remain.

You enter the living room.
The envelope is addressed to Mrs. Marshall Robner. It bears a July 6, 1982 postmark.

“Dear Leslie,

I am sorry to hear that Marshall is despondent again. I know how much his troubles weigh on you, and I wish I could be there to comfort you. His despondency is tied to his business. He speaks of suicide when he is in this state, but the thought of what will happen to the company may keep him going.

So George has made his threats again? It is hard to believe he could cause Marshall so much pain. If the worst should happen, you will be provided for as you deserve.

I look forward to Friday, when we can be together again. Until then, remember how much I love you and the life we hope to share.

Love,
Steven”

events.message: “I don't know much about that.”
